When Vision Needs a Second Look: Tool-Augmented Iterative Perception for Earth Observation

Atul Dev* Shivank Garg* Gaurav Kumar Nayak†

atul_d@ma.iitr.ac.in   |   shivank_g@mfs.iitr.ac.in   |   gauravkumar.nayak@mfs.iitr.ac.in

Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Roorkee

* Equal contribution    † Corresponding author

OpenReview Paper PPT Poster
Abstract

Earth Observation (EO) uses satellite and aerial imagery to monitor the Earth’s surface, supporting critical applications in infrastructure, agriculture, and climate change. As governments and industry scale EO pipelines, reliable automation has become essential. Yet, current Vision-Language Models are limited to coarse-grained perception, struggling to execute the precise, multi-step reasoning required for real-world Earth observation tasks. Recent evaluations on benchmarks like GeoBench-VLM highlight this shortcoming: even state-of-the-art models show low accuracy and frequently struggle with tasks requiring precise numerical reasoning and domain-specific knowledge, such as object counting, crop-type classification, and assessing vegetation health.

To address these limitations, we introduce GeoScout-Agent, an autonomous agentic framework that couples GPT-5-mini with progressive zooming, sharpening, code execution, DINOv3, and SAM3. The model iteratively decomposes, validates, and refines its predictions rather than relying on a single forward pass. Evaluated on GeoBench-VLM, GeoScout-Agent achieves a relative 17.3% improvement across the evaluated tasks over the baseline approach.

Overview

GeoScout-Agent uses tools inside the reasoning loop.

Given an image and a question, the agent can inspect the evidence, call a specialized tool, and continue until it has a final response.

Failure case

Single-pass inference fails in dense scenes.

Despite generating a plausible and internally consistent reasoning trace, the base GPT-5-mini model produces an incorrect count due to occlusion, object adjacency, and limited visual resolution. This highlights the brittleness of single-pass inference without explicit visual verification.

Example

Iterative visual verification recovers the correct count.

GeoScout-Agent incrementally refines its hypothesis through object discovery, segmentation, and targeted zooming, enabling reliable instance separation in a cluttered scene.

Results

GeoScout-Agent improves accuracy across object-count ranges.

The chart compares GeoScout-GPT5mini with GPT-5-mini and other vision-language baselines on GeoBench-VLM. GeoScout-GPT5mini achieves the highest accuracy in every object-count range shown, with the largest gap over GPT-5-mini in the 30-40 object range.

Relative improvement GeoScout-GPT5mini over the tool-free GPT-5-mini baseline Absolute accuracy: 52.0% to 61.0% (+9.0 percentage points)
34.5%
Relative improvement GeoScout-Qwen3 over tool-free Qwen3-VL Absolute accuracy: 41.2% to 55.4% (+14.2 percentage points)

Counting tasks. GeoScout-GPT5mini improves building counting by 17.6 percentage points (+67.95% relative), tree counting by 31.8 points (+122.78%), water-body counting by 25.9 points (+78.72%), and general vehicle counting by 22.0 points (+78.57%). GeoScout-Qwen3 improves general aircraft counting from 32.3% to 61.9% (+91.64% relative), general vehicle counting from 31.3% to 57.9% (+84.98%), and tree counting from 41.7% to 58.2% (+39.57%).
